clue.text: Force to speak to an audience

indicators.note: something said to an audience is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to speak is to talk

explanation.surface: Someone is being compelled to give a speech to a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb ('compel'), but it is the noun from physics, a twisting force.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is the rotational force that turns an axle or a bolt.

clue.text: Bachelor, old one, and girlfriend maybe get too passionate

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a girlfriend is one example of a lover

explanation.surface: A single man, his elderly friend and his girlfriend all lose their tempers.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil over is an idiom for emotions spilling out uncontrollably, like a pan on the stove.

clue.text: Model railway's set out

parts.note: a model of car is its make
a railway has tracks, the 's standing for has

explanation.surface: Someone's model railway layout has been arranged on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as 'laid out', describing the model, but it means 'departed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make tracks is an idiom for leaving or setting off on a journey.

clue.text: Tripe that noisy person's ordered

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses as rubbish the meal a loud diner has chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as an instruction: what a noisy person is ordered is 'To (them): Sh!', so TO SH. 'Tripe' looks like offal on a menu but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for nonsense or rubbish, the same as tripe.

clue.text: Vital passage from Le Cid, but in translation

indicators.note: a translation recasts the words, so the letters here are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A key passage from Corneille's play Le Cid, but read in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital passage' sounds like a crucial bit of text, but it is a channel in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The bile duct is a tube in the body carrying bile from liver to gut, a vital channel.

clue.text: Folly of decorative material houses one locally

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lacy means made of lace, a decorative fabric
'un is a dialect form of one

explanation.surface: Some lace-like ornament or folly in an old house contains a local item.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy means madness, a strong word for foolish behaviour or folly.

clue.text: Not a shrub seen regularly in Pacific location

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter of the words is picked

explanation.surface: A plant that is not a shrub is a common sight in some Pacific spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island that holds Honolulu, in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: What's to stop one burning paper flower?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
the flower of something is its best part, its cream

explanation.surface: Asking what would stop a paper flower from catching fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom (or, in crosswords, a river), but here it means the pick or best of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun cream is a lotion applied to the skin to prevent sunburn.

clue.text: Ceremony, endlessly gloomy, in which one's installed president once

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
one is I, the Roman numeral, with 's for is

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dour means stern and gloomy

explanation.surface: A gloomy ceremony at which someone is sworn in as a former head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's installed' reads as part of the ceremony's story, a person sworn in, but it just puts the numeral one inside the shortened gloomy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Pompidou was President of France from 1969 to 1974.

clue.text: Giant blunder by one defending teaching of religion

parts.note: an own goal, OG, is the classic blunder by a defender in football
RE is religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A huge mistake made by someone defending religious instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folklore that eats people.

clue.text: Volunteers check in a couple of Latin exercises

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: one piece set inside another

parts.note: two in Latin numerals is II
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Volunteers checking a pair of Latin exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) was the British army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese system of slow, flowing physical exercises.

clue.text: College type studied — but not a reliable colleague?

indicators.note: but not means except for, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a brick is a dependable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A kind of college someone studied at, but not a trustworthy co-worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like part of 'a reliable colleague', but it is the letter removed from READ. A redbrick is one of the British universities founded in industrial cities around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbrick describes the civic British universities, a type distinct from Oxbridge colleges.

clue.text: Baker, workmanlike, turning around sandwiches

indicators.note: turning around means the letters run backwards
a sandwich holds its filling inside, so the letters are found within the word

explanation.surface: A baker, working steadily, turns around some sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like a person, but it is a thing that bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is an oven for firing pottery, so in a sense a baker of clay.

clue.text: More than happy to thrash out non-PC issue

indicators.note: thrashing something out works it over hard, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: Glad to discuss a politically incorrect topic thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in one's cups means being drunk, which is jokingly 'more than happy', merry.

clue.text: Give out fine for concealing note: what's often proper

indicators.note: to conceal is to hold something hidden inside

parts.note: ace means excellent, fine
a noun is often a proper noun, a name

explanation.surface: A fine is imposed for hiding a banknote, as is often right.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to proclaim or declare publicly, to give out news.

clue.text: Expressions of gratitude by crew for old navigator

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you, so tas are thanks
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Thanks are given by the ship's crew to an old navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was a 17th-century Dutch explorer who reached Tasmania and New Zealand.

clue.text: African leaves fancier sort of beer, put out and upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: IPA is India pale ale, a type of beer
KO, a knockout, puts a boxer out

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their fancy beer, knocked out and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, but the definition is a fancier (lover) of leaves, an animal from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of Central Africa, related to the giraffe, that browses on foliage.

clue.text: Advance position unfairly, having declared prompt start

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a cue is a prompt for an actor
to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gains an unfair edge by announcing they will begin on time.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue-jump is to push ahead of others waiting, unfairly improving one's place.

clue.text: Visibly upset, with head giving out reprimand

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, gives out, failing and dropping away

parts.note: tearful means crying, visibly upset

explanation.surface: Someone visibly distressed, their head exhausted, gives a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long, angry telling-off, a scolding.

clue.text: Starting all over, can request a book for training

indicators.note: training puts something through drills and reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may borrow a book about training.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to square one is an idiom for having to begin again from the start.

clue.text: Where some Channel water is fresh

definitions.meaning: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, so its water is in that strait

explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the stretch of the English Channel between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire. 'fresh' looks like the opposite of salt water but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and disrespectful, the cheeky sense of fresh.

clue.text: Surgery can be involved voluntarily

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: An operation may be something one chooses to take part in.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt in is to choose to take part in a scheme by one's own decision.

clue.text: I start to relax with a piece of cake and tea here?

definitions.text: I start to relax with a piece of cake and tea here?

parts.note: something that is a piece of cake is easy
cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone settles down to unwind with cake and a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a comfortable armchair, just where one relaxes with cake and tea.

clue.text: Helping after a party brings enormous respect

indicators.note: one piece comes after another in the answer

parts.note: a do is a party
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Assisting after a party earns someone great esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and reverence, far beyond ordinary respect.

clue.text: Expressed regret over attempts to extract fuel for car parts

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to rue is to regret
to frack is to fracture rock to release gas or oil

explanation.surface: Someone voiced regret about drilling for fuel to make car components.
explanation.definitionFit: Roof racks are frames fixed on top of a car to carry luggage.

clue.text: Rider cycles initially out of habit

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: an addiction is a compulsive habit

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: A cyclist begins by riding just out of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' looks like a cyclist but is a legal term for a clause added to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added on to a bill or contract, an extra.

clue.text: Lines street taking in duke beating "stranger"?

indicators.note: taking in means containing, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: A poem about a street in which a duke beats up a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beating "stranger"' means going one degree beyond the comparative, to the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Going one beyond the comparative of odd gives its superlative, so most strange beats stranger.

clue.text: African runner needing reason not to pass

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
to go is to pass, as in a turn in a game

explanation.surface: An African athlete needs a good reason not to pass the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete but in crosswords is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a great river of Central Africa, and rivers run.

clue.text: Film director imposing limit on artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A film director places restrictions on an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Capra was the Hollywood film director of It's a Wonderful Life.
